essentialIdeas: Phospholipid bilayers create selective permeability because hydrophilic heads face water and hydrophobic tails form a barrier to many polar or charged substances.

activities.label: membrane_model
activities.title: Membrane structure model
activities.body: Review the model, then identify the key relationship in one sentence.

essentialIdeas: Phospholipid bilayers create selective permeability because hydrophilic heads face water and hydrophobic tails form a barrier to many polar or charged substances.
Passive transport moves substances down a concentration gradient without energy, while active transport requires energy to move substances against that gradient.

activities.label: explain_transport
activities.title: Explain transport in your own words
activities.body: Explain the two membrane ideas in your own words. Keep it to 2 to 4 sentences.
activities.concept: Explain how phospholipid structure creates selective permeability
activities.correctAnswer: The phospholipid bilayer has hydrophilic heads facing water and hydrophobic tails in the middle, so it blocks many polar or charged substances. Passive transport moves down a concentration gradient without energy, while active transport uses energy to move against the gradient.
activities.feedback: A complete answer states both why the bilayer is selective and how passive differs from active transport. If missing, add the role of hydrophobic tails and the energy direction.

activities.label: repair_gap
activities.title: Repair the membrane rule
activities.body: Revise your explanation using the correction below. Then give one improved sentence.
activities.correctAnswer: Passive transport moves down a concentration gradient without energy, and active transport requires energy to move against the gradient.
activities.feedback: Fix any answer that says active transport is passive or that energy is needed for both. The corrected rule is about gradient direction and energy use.

activities.label: reexplain_model
activities.title: State the membrane model again
activities.body: Explain the full membrane model again in plain language. Do not copy the earlier wording.
activities.concept: Explain how phospholipid structure creates selective permeability
activities.correctAnswer: Phospholipid bilayers are selective because their hydrophobic interior blocks many polar or charged substances, while the heads face water. Passive transport goes down a gradient without energy, and active transport uses energy to move against a gradient.
activities.feedback: Your second explanation should be accurate and independent. Include both the membrane barrier and the energy difference between passive and active transport.

activities.label: transport_check
activities.title: Classify a transport example
activities.body: Choose the best answer for the transport example.
choices: A substance moves from high concentration to low concentration without energy
A substance moves from low concentration to high concentration using energy
A membrane breaks apart to let everything pass freely
A substance moves only because the cell makes more of it
activities.correctAnswer: A substance moves from low concentration to high concentration using energy
activities.feedback: Active transport requires energy because it moves against the concentration gradient. The other choices describe diffusion, an impossible membrane change, or an unsupported cause.

items.essentialIdea: Phospholipid bilayers allow small nonpolar molecules to pass more easily than ions.

check.title: Bilayer permeability
check.prompt: Why do phospholipid bilayers let some substances cross more easily than others?
check.referenceAnswer: The bilayer’s hydrophobic interior permits small nonpolar molecules to pass more easily, while charged particles and polar molecules are restricted.
check.feedback: The hydrophobic core blocks many polar or charged substances, so permeability is selective.

items.essentialIdea: Passive transport moves substances down gradients without cellular energy, while active transport uses energy against gradients.

check.title: Transport direction and energy
check.prompt: How do passive transport and active transport differ in direction relative to a gradient and energy use?
check.referenceAnswer: Passive transport goes down a concentration gradient and does not require cellular energy. Active transport moves against a gradient and requires energy.
check.feedback: The key difference is both direction and energy use: passive is downhill, active is uphill.

recognitionCheck.title: Choose active transport
recognitionCheck.prompt: Which statement best describes active transport?
choices: It moves substances against a concentration gradient and requires cellular energy.
It moves substances down a concentration gradient without cellular energy.
It only allows small nonpolar molecules to cross the membrane.
It occurs only when no concentration gradient exists.
recognitionCheck.correctAnswer: It moves substances against a concentration gradient and requires cellular energy.
recognitionCheck.feedback: Active transport is the energy-requiring, uphill form of membrane transport.
